claim.value: Elevated weekly late-start rates in consecutive weeks are a temporal pattern to seek.
claim.scope: A prospective observation category; the baseline or threshold defining an elevated rate is unspecified.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans identify consecutive elevated weekly rates as a pattern to seek and explicitly characterize the signals as prospective observations.

signal_basis.value: Record turnaround events comparably, review daily, and summarize weekly late bookings divided by all bookings, displaying booking denominators and missing-record counts. Seek elevated rates across consecutive weeks.
signal_basis.scope: A prospective temporal observation using consistent start definitions; collection is not equated with actual start unless their relationship is verified. No numerical elevation threshold is specified.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply comparable recording, start-definition safeguards, weekly rate construction, reporting context, and the prospective pattern.
No unresolved empirical relation is needed to license this bounded observation-category claim.

rationale: Consecutive weekly rate observations constitute a temporal sequence, and repeated elevation is a temporal pattern within it. The claim only identifies a pattern to seek; it asserts neither an observed finding nor a causal or statistical conclusion.
uncertainty: The unspecified elevation baseline limits how the category can be operationalized, but does not undermine this explicitly bounded claim.
